ozet: In front of the sundial on Discovery Island, Piko explains the datetime module: creating dates, formatting them with strftime, and counting days between dates.

giris.anlatim: Day 16: Dates and times! In this lesson you'll create dates with the datetime module, format them, and count the days between dates.

cikis.anlatim: The interactive version of this lesson is waiting for you at 30gunde.com.tr. Write your code right in the browser, run it instantly, and finish the tasks!
maddeler: Write and run code in your browser
Learn Python step by step in 30 days

sahneler.anlatim: Hi, I'm Piko! We've set foot on Discovery Island. In the middle of the island there's a giant sundial, and on it is written: whoever reads the time solves the island's secret. How do you think daily streaks in games are counted? Today we read time with Python!
For dates and times we use the datetime module. Three parts do the job: date holds a date, datetime holds a date and a time together, and timedelta is the length of time between two moments.

ekran.kod:
from datetime import date, datetime, timedelta

today = date.today()      # today's date
now = datetime.now()      # the current date and time

sahneler.anlatim: Careful: date.today gives a different result every day. So in the examples we'll use fixed dates, and the outputs will always stay the same.

maddeler: Fixed date in the examples: date(2026, 9, 23)

sahneler.anlatim: To make a date, I write the year, the month and the day, in that order. Then I take its parts one by one with year, month and day. On the last line, strftime turns the date into familiar-looking text.

ekran.kod:
from datetime import date

d = date(2026, 9, 23)
print("Year:", d.year)
print("Month:", d.month)
print("Day:", d.day)
print(d.strftime("%d.%m.%Y"))

sahneler.anlatim: The letters with percent signs inside strftime are placeholders: percent d is the day, percent m the month, and capital Y the four-digit year. strptime does the opposite: it reads text and makes a real date out of it.

ekran.kod:
from datetime import datetime

t = datetime.strptime("23.09.2026", "%d.%m.%Y")
print(t)
print(t.strftime("%d/%m/%Y"))

sahneler.anlatim: Now it's time to count. When I subtract today from New Year's Day, I get the time in between. The .days at the end turns that into a number of days. Exactly one hundred days!

ekran.kod:
from datetime import date

today = date(2026, 9, 23)
new_year = date(2027, 1, 1)
left = (new_year - today).days
print(f"{left} days until the new year.")

sahneler.anlatim: To add days to a date, I use timedelta. Each round, the loop adds seven, fourteen and twenty-one days. When the month runs out, Python moves on to the next month by itself.

ekran.kod:
from datetime import date, timedelta

start = date(2026, 9, 23)
for week in range(1, 4):
    later = start + timedelta(days=7 * week)
    print(f"Week {week}:", later.strftime("%d.%m.%Y"))

sahneler.anlatim: The most common mistake is writing a date that isn't on the calendar. There's no February thirtieth! Python gives a ValueError and says the day is out of range for the month.

ekran.baslik: Common mistake: a date that doesn't exist
ekran.kod:
from datetime import date

d = date(2026, 2, 30)
ekran.cikti: ValueError: day is out of range for month

sahneler.anlatim: Now it's your turn. I'm subtracting two dates, but I forgot to write .days. What do you think this code prints?

ekran.kod:
from datetime import date

print(date(2026, 9, 30) - date(2026, 9, 1))

sahneler.anlatim: The result isn't a number, it's a length of time: twenty-nine days and zero hours. If you only need the number of days, don't forget to add .days at the end.

ekran.kod:
from datetime import date

print(date(2026, 9, 30) - date(2026, 9, 1))

sahneler.anlatim: Task time! First you'll print a date as day, month and year. Then you'll find how many days are left until your birthday, and finally you'll add weeks to a date. In the project, you're building the daily streak system.
In short: build a date with date, write it nicely with strftime, and subtract two dates to do math with timedelta.

maddeler: Make a date with date(year, month, day)
Turn it into text with strftime, back into a date with strptime
Date difference with .days, add days with timedelta
